name: HE Solkan
zag_role: Expansive and non-shrink cements for grout concrete (introduced by ZRMK), technical observation of the dam
description: ZAG's 2024 book states that ZRMK, the predecessor of ZAG, introduced its non-shrink and expansive cements for grout concrete when HE Solkan was built. The same book lists the Solkan dam among the dams under ZAG technical observation.
history: HE Solkan is the lowest of the large plants on the Soča, standing roughly 700 m upstream of the Solkan railway bridge. It is a run of river plant with three Kaplan units, a combined swallowing capacity of 180 cubic metres per second and a gross head of 20.55 m at a flow of 60 cubic metres per second. The reservoir holds about 1.15 million cubic metres of useful storage, the permitted water level fluctuation is 1.5 m, and the catchment is 1,632 square kilometres. Average annual generation is about 105 GWh. In July 2022 the plant stopped generating entirely because of the low flow of the Soča. The operator brochure records that a reconstruction is planned for after 2025.

source_differences: Useful storage: record/brochure 1,150,000 m3 (SENG brochure) vs 1,000,000 m3 'effective storage capacity' on SENG large-HPP web page.
Installed capacity: record 32.4 MW (3 x 10.8 MW, brochure) vs 32 MW on SENG web page, OpenInfraMap and en.wikipedia list (rounding).

ZAG role: the ZAG book of 2024 credits ZRMK, the predecessor of ZAG, with non-shrink cements for the construction of this plant. Wording in the record that goes beyond that, such as cable duct grouting or ZAG grout formulations, was not found in the part of the book that could be read.
